# Three kinds of muscle

<!-- STEP id="voluntary" -->
## Movements you control
Some movements happen only when you choose to make them, such as running, writing or lifting a bag. These are called **voluntary movements**.

<!-- STEP id="skeletal" -->
## Skeletal muscle
Voluntary movements are made by **skeletal muscles**, which are attached to the skeleton. A skeletal muscle is made of bundles of long, cylindrical cells called muscle fibres. Each fibre is unbranched and has many nuclei, and it shows light and dark bands called striations.

<!-- STEP id="involuntary" -->
## Movements that happen on their own
Food moves along your intestine and your heart beats without any thought from you. These are called **involuntary movements**, and two other kinds of muscle make them.

<!-- STEP id="smooth" -->
## Smooth muscle
**Smooth muscle** is found in organs such as the stomach and the intestines. Its cells are spindle-shaped, which means thick in the middle and pointed at both ends. Each cell has a single nucleus and no striations. Smooth muscle makes slow, continuous movements, such as the movements of digestion.

<!-- STEP id="cardiac" -->
## Cardiac muscle
**Cardiac muscle** is found only in the heart. Its fibres are cylindrical and branched, each has a single nucleus, and the striations are faint. Cardiac muscle works rhythmically and without tiring, so the heart beats throughout life without fatigue.

<!-- STEP id="compare" -->
## Side by side

| Muscle | Cells | Nuclei | Bands |
|---|---|---|---|
| Skeletal | long, unbranched | many | yes |
| Smooth | spindle | one | no |
| Cardiac | branched | one | faint |

| Muscle | Where | Control |
|---|---|---|
| Skeletal | on bones | voluntary |
| Smooth | stomach, gut | involuntary |
| Cardiac | heart only | involuntary |

**Each kind of muscle has its own cell shape, its own place in the body and its own kind of movement.**
